resumen: With the torso hinged and the upper arm against your side, the elbow opens backwards. The triceps works shortened.
ejecucion: Hinge your torso forward with a flat back and your elbows against your sides.
Start with the elbow bent to 90° and the dumbbell hanging.
Straighten the elbow, taking the dumbbell back, without moving the upper arm.
The upper arm must stay still: the only thing that moves is the forearm.
matices: With the arm at your side the long head of the triceps starts shortened, so it contributes less than in the overhead version — that is what the cited study measures. In exchange, the hardest point falls at the end of the range, with the elbow straight.
